source.title: Natural Spectral Fusion: p-Exponent Cyclic Scheduling and Early Decision-Boundary Alignment in First-Order Optimization

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether changing the optimizer’s second-moment exponent and schedule affects held-out performance, using methods different from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Reports its own test-accuracy and validation-accuracy results for p-exponent settings and p-tidal scheduling. The cited optimizer comparisons in Related Work are not results from this study. The text does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected models, batch size, dropout, generalization measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: Section 3.3 explicitly compares SGD (p=0) and Adam-style normalization (p=0.5) on held-out image accuracy with other settings fixed, bearing on V4. The supplied text does not resolve their pairwise accuracy differences. The proposed schedule's performance alone does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is partly accurate but overstates loss improvement. The authors conclude that exponent scheduling broadens spectral coverage and improves TinyImageNet accuracy under identical learning-rate policies, without necessarily reducing loss. Their abstract makes broader error/loss and efficiency claims than the detailed experiment establishes.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces second-moment exponent extension and cyclic p scheduling; its TinyImageNet comparison uses a fixed-p SGD endpoint, rather than the interventions in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the reported p-performance trend. In TinyImageNet, the p-tidal schedule improves accuracy while test loss does not show a comparable reduction.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed pulse–tidal schedule raises TinyImageNet validation accuracy from 59.1% to 62.9% against fixed-p SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cyclic second-moment exponent scheduling can improve held-out classification accuracy over fixed-p SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation accuracy improves sooner without a comparable reduction in test loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exponent scheduling can improve classification accuracy without proportionate improvement in cross-entropy loss.

record.problems: The supplied text reports one real-world scheduling experiment on TinyImageNet with ResNet-18; the stated three-run variance applies to the proposed accuracy result. Preliminary dataset trends lack recoverable numeric values in the text. Fig. 6 test-loss values are figure-only, and the textual timing estimates differ between Results and Discussion. The paper describes the spectral mapping as heuristic rather than exact.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Learning-rate and decay-schedule tuning comparisons, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, Adam-to-SGD switching, language benchmarks, and comparable training performance. Section 3.3 instead holds other settings fixed while varying p.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Separate p=0 and p=0.5 held-out accuracies for each dataset, with their fixed training settings. R1 acknowledges these configurations but does not capture their comparison, preventing a directional V4 verdict.
missing.locator: Section 3.3 and Figure 1; referenced hyperparameter appendix is absent from the supplied text

record.verdict_notes: No directional V4 verdict is justified from the readable endpoint results. Positive-p advantages or intermediate-p optima do not by themselves establish Adam versus SGD ordering. The spectral interpretation is explicitly heuristic.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers such as Adam versus SGD under the tuning conditions described.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring its effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared p-exponent settings on multiple datasets; the reported text summarizes dataset-specific test-accuracy trends.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, Chaoyang, RAFDB, FER2013
varied; exact settings not stated in the result summary

rows.value: FER2013 shows a clear advantage for positive p; CIFAR-10 and RAFDB can benefit from smaller or negative p; TinyImageNet, Chaoyang, and CIFAR-100 have one or more intermediate-p peaks.
rows.note: The text gives qualitative trends but no corresponding numerical values; Fig. 1 is not sufficiently legible in the supplied text to recover values.
rows.check: The experiment includes both SGD and Adam endpoints, so it bears on V4. However, the aggregated dataset trends do not establish which endpoint generalizes better; endpoint accuracies cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with fixed p = 0 as the SGD-endpoint baseline.
rows.note: The proposed schedule is the comparator; the text reports variance within ±0.2% across three runs for the proposed result, not separately for this baseline.
rows.check: This is a baseline for the proposed schedule, without an Adam comparison. The reported 59.1% is validation accuracy in the described experiment.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with fixed p = 0 as the SGD-endpoint baseline.
rows.note: The figure plots test loss; no exact values or textual comparison are given.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Used pulse–tidal scheduling, with p = −0.05 in the pulse phase and tidal values alternating between 0.25 and −0.15 every 200 iterations.
rows.note: The paper reports the accuracy comparison directly.
rows.check: The 59.1% to 62.9% validation-accuracy improvement measures the proposed schedule against SGD, rather than the optimizer comparison V4 names. Observed is inappropriate as a claim-version state.

rows.subject: ResNet-18

rows.check: Convergence speed for the proposed method does not measure a listed version. The 15–20% and 75% timing estimates conflict.
